explanation.text: The congressional pay amendment was proposed on September 25, 1789, along with the original Bill of Rights amendments.
The original Bill of Rights amendments were ratified by three-fourths of the states on December 15, 1791.
The congressional pay amendment was ratified on May 7, 1992, after more than 202 years from its proposal.
The time between proposal and ratification for the congressional pay amendment was approximately 202.5 years.
The time between proposal and ratification for the original Bill of Rights amendments was approximately 2 years and 3 months.
The congressional pay amendment took significantly longer to ratify than the original Bill of Rights amendments.

excerpts.text: The article on Congressional compensation was initially ratified by seven states through 1792 (including Kentucky), but was not ratified by another state for eighty years. The [Ohio General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_General_Assembly "Ohio General Assembly") ratified it on May 6, 1873, in protest of an unpopular [Congressional pay raise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salary_Grab_Act "Salary Grab Act").[[14]](#cite_note-dean-14) A century later, on March 6, 1978, the [Wyoming Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming_Legislature "Wyoming Legislature") also ratified the article.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

He discovered in 1983 that Ohio had approved the amendment in 1873 as a means of protest against the [Salary Grab Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salary_Grab_Act "Salary Grab Act") and learned in 1984 that Wyoming had done the same in 1978, as a protest against a 1977 congressional pay raise.[[14]](#cite_note-dean-14)[[23]](#cite_note-23) Watson also did not know until 1997, well after the amendment's adoption, that Kentucky had ratified the amendment in 1792.[[24]](#cite_note-24) Neither did Kentucky lawmakers themselves – in Watson's desire for a 50-state sweep, the Kentucky General Assembly post-ratified the amendment in 1996 (Senate Joint Resolution No. 50), at Watson's request, likewise unaware that the task had already been attended to 204 years earlier.[[25]](#cite_note-25)
Kentucky's then-unknown 1792 ratification would have made it 41 states that had ratified at the time of certification, three more than the 38 required for a three-quarters majority.

On May 20, 1992, under the authority recognized in *Coleman*, and in keeping with the precedent established by [the ratification of the Fourteenth Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution#Adoption "Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution"), each house of the 102nd Congress passed its own version of a [concurrent resolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrent_resolution "Concurrent resolution") agreeing that the amendment was validly ratified, despite the more than 202 years the task took.

excerpts.text: On September 25, 1789, after Congress approved the Congressional Pay Amendment by a vote of two-thirds of both Houses, it was submitted to the states as [one of twelve proposed amendments](https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/bill-of-rights) to the Constitution, including the 10 proposals that would later become the Bill of Rights. By the end of 1791, 6 of the then-existing 14 states [had ratified](https://digitalcommons.nyls.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1459&context=fac_articles_chapters#page=37) the Pay Amendment, leaving it short of the 11 state legislatures needed to constitute a three-fourths majority for purposes of ratification at the time.

From the mid-1980s to the early 1990s, more than 30 state legislatures [ratified the Amendment](https://digitalcommons.nyls.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1459&context=fac_articles_chapters#page=43), responding to public opposition to congressional pay increases.

Wilson, on the advice of attorneys in the Department of Justice's Office of Legal Counsel, [proclaimed](https://archives.federalregister.gov/issue_slice/1992/5/19/21187-21188.pdf#page=1) the Amendment to have been ratified on May 7, 1992.
